results.note: Reproduced in fresh Playwright contexts at 1440x900 (DPR 1) and 390x844 (iPhone UA, DPR 2) with CDP Network capture. At both viewports exactly two video requests fire on load, each a single Range: bytes=0- request answered 206 with the whole file: https://roscap.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Roscap+Video++(1).mp4 (Content-Range 0-6766235/6766236, encodedDataLength 6,766,706 bytes, Server: AmazonS3, no CDN headers, requested at ~0.63 s, finished at ~1.39 s on the fast test link) and the Webflow MP4 cdn.prod.website-files.com/...Roscap%20Video%20%20%281%29_mp4.mp4 (Content-Range 0-1553966/1553967, 1,554,733 bytes, Cloudflare). Total page encoded bytes 10,161,712 (desktop) and 10,083,431 (mobile), so the two videos are 82 percent of the page. The Webflow element .hero-bg.hide.w-background-video is display:none yet its video reports readyState 4, buffered [0,17.7] and paused=true: fully downloaded, never shown. The custom-embed video has no poster attribute and no preload attribute. ffprobe on the first 2 MB of the S3 file: h264 1440x1078, 24 fps, 17.69 s, moov atom at byte 32 (faststart). This Chromium build reports canPlayType avc1 = probably and the S3 video reached readyState 4 and played, so the measurement is not a codec artefact. Lighthouse JSON (same Chromium) independently records transferSize 6,766,687 and 1,556,067 for the two files on both mobile and desktop runs, mobile performance 66, LCP 5.8 s. One nuance: under CDP throttling at 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT the S3 video was still at readyState 1 (metadata only, no frame) 10 s after navigation at both viewports, which is worse than the auditor's 'complete at 4.0 s' on a fast connection. Severity high is fair.

Reproduced with page.route aborting *.mp4, *.webm and the S3 host (3 requests blocked per load). Computed styles at both viewports: .section.is-heroheader background-color rgba(0,0,0,0) and background-image none, .main-wrapper rgba(0,0,0,0), body rgb(255,252,245) (#FFFCF5), h1 colour rgb(255,255,255), hero paragraph rgb(255,255,255); at 1440 the visible nav links (.nav-links.w-nav-link) are also rgb(255,255,255). No element inside the hero has an opaque background except the gold button (rgb(225,201,121)); the only poster is the background-image on the hidden Webflow video, which is display:none. Screenshots ha02-home-d1440-novideo-fold.png and ha02-home-m390-novideo-fold.png show a cream block with ghost-white headline and paragraph, only the logo and gold button legible. Not just a simulation: the Lighthouse filmstrip for Home mobile (lh-home-mobile-thumb0-512ms.png) shows exactly this state at 512 ms on an unthrottled connection, with the video frame appearing by 1,024 ms; the desktop filmstrip shows blank then video by 1,031 ms. Under CDP throttling at 1.6 Mbps the video was still readyState 1 (no frame decoded) at 1.5, 3, 6 and 10 s, so the headline stayed unreadable for more than 10 s (ha02-home-m390-throttled-6000ms.png). Confirmed at severity high.

Fresh context (no cookies, no storage), first load, no interaction, both pages at 1440 and 390: 3 Google requests every time (www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-H8HS2R6NLS, analytics.google.com/g/collect, stats.g.doubleclick.net/g/collect). Cookies set by the end of load: _ga (GA1.1.449459387...) and _ga_H8HS2R6NLS, both on .roscap.co.uk with expiry about 400 days out, plus Cloudflare's _cfuvid. Inline head code calls gtag('config','G-H8HS2R6NLS') immediately; zero gtag('consent', ...) calls in any script; the collect hits carry no gcs parameter and gcd=13l3l3l3l1l1 (no consent defaults configured). localStorage is empty. DOM scan for id/class containing cookie, consent, gdpr, cc-, banner, aria-label cookie or role=dialog: on Home the only match is .contact-banner-wrap (a contact CTA), on About Us the two team role=dialog popups; nothing is a consent UI. The word cookie appears only in the footer link to /cookie-policy. The approved in-house banner is not live. Under the brief's own scale (compliance risk = critical) the severity is fair for a UK site that sets analytics cookies before consent.

Reproduced at 1440 and 390 with real key presses. Tabbing onto the first .team-popup-trigger (role=button, tabindex=0, id='Suleman Rafiq') and pressing Enter opens the dialog (display flex); focus lands on the first .team-popup-social-card link (mailto:suleman@roscap.co.uk). 12 further Tabs all land on A.team-popup-social-card inside the dialog (the two links alternate); 3 Shift+Tabs likewise. Escape leaves both dialogs' display unchanged (not closed). 20 more Tabs never reach the close control. The close control is with no role, tabindex, aria-label or title, parent is a DIV, so it is not focusable (programmatic focus() also fails); a mouse click on it does close the dialog, so this is a keyboard-only failure. Static checks: 2 elements share id='fs-modal-1-popup'; aria-labelledby='fs-modal-1-heading' points to no element (the dialog h3 has no id); trigger ids are 'Suleman Rafiq' and 'Clemente M. Apollonj-Ghetti'; aria-expanded stays 'false' while open; no inert and no aria-hidden on the rest of the page. The open/close logic is the inline script after the CodeSandbox tag (click handlers only, no keydown handler); Finsweet attributes-a11y supplies the Enter activation and focus trapping. A dialog that keyboard users cannot leave is a WCAG 2.1.2 (Level A) failure; critical is fair. Screenshot ha04-about-d1440-dialog-open.png.

All facts reproduce: About Us loads <script src='https://jj59l3.csb.app/script.js'> synchronously before the inline modal script; curl and CDP both return HTTP 200, Content-Type text/javascript, 1,486 bytes (981 to 1,213 gzip-encoded), Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, no-cache, no-store, Server: cloudflare, Via: 1.1 google, so it is re-fetched from a new origin on every load (Lighthouse mobile: request 415 ms to 1,676 ms). Content is a GSAP counter (power3.out, no loop) targeting .stats-cards-wrap/.stats-num-span and a Swiper init on .slider-wrap .swiper; on About Us these selectors match 0 elements (Home uses a different inline copy with circ.in/power2 and loop:true), no console errors or page errors, so the script does nothing. The inline Finsweet a11y loader does appear in each of the 2 CMS team items but it checks for an existing tag first, so a11y.js is loaded once (1 tag). Severity: the script is inert today and the risk (third-party dev-sandbox script with no SRI, extra origin, delays DOMContentLoaded and therefore the modal click handlers) is latent rather than something that clearly hurts users now, so medium rather than high. Removal recommendation stands.

axe-core (fresh contexts, both pages, 1440 and 390, after scrolling the page): input-button-name, impact critical, 1 node every run: <input type='submit' data-wait='' class='footer-submit w-button' value=''>. The footer email input has placeholder only (Home: id=email, placeholder 'Email'; About: id=Email, placeholder 'Email Address'), no <label for>, not wrapped in a label, no aria-label; axe does not flag it because placeholder counts as a name, but there is no visible label. Playwright's getByRole('button', {name: ''}) also finds it. Lighthouse accessibility 85 (Home) and 88 (About) match the summary. Severity high is fair for an unnamed form control present site-wide. Related, not in the finding: axe color-contrast (serious) on the footer .text-color-grey2 copyright and disclaimer paragraphs on both pages and on the Home .slider-heading.is-inactive at opacity 0.4.

axe link-name (serious): 4 nodes at 1440 and 5 at 390 on both pages, exactly as claimed. Nodes: a.nav_brand-2 (href '/', logo img alt='', the second img 'BE Logo White' sits in a hidden wrapper so the link has no name), a[href='mailto:info@roscap.co.uk'].social-link, the LinkedIn .social-link and the Instagram .social-link (all three contain SVGs with no title, role or aria-label and no text), plus at 390 a.nav_button-2 href='#' (Lottie hamburger, no aria-label, no aria-expanded, no role); the Webflow-native .w-nav-button that does carry aria-label='menu' is hidden (offsetWidth 0) so it does not help. Instagram href is https://www.instagram.com/roscap.uk?igsh=MXM1OXRtbDhiYTUx (share token present). Severity high is fair: the home link and the only mobile menu control have no accessible name.

Rendered at 390x844, DPR 2, iPhone UA: img.hero-bg has loading='lazy', no fetchpriority, sizes='(max-width: 1924px) 100vw, 1924px'; the browser chose the 800w candidate (new%20hero%20bg-p-800.avif, intrinsic 800x533 px, 28,492 bytes, CDP priority Low, parser-initiated, requested at 420 ms after a 436 ms FCP, finished 675 ms). It is position absolute, object-fit cover, rendered at 390x844 CSS px = 780x1688 device px, so the cover scale is max(780/800, 1688/533) = 3.17x (auditor said 3.26x; same order, height-limited because a landscape 3:2 image fills a portrait viewport). Desktop 1440 uses the 1924w file (87,201 bytes) at 0.75x, no upscaling. Lighthouse 13.6 JSON about-us-mobile.json: lcp-discovery-insight names img.hero-bg (boundingRect 412x823) as the LCP element and fails both 'LCP resources shouldn't use loading=lazy' and 'fetchpriority=high should be applied'; lcp-breakdown shows resource load delay 412 ms (mobile) and 455 ms (desktop), the cost of the lazy attribute; metric LCP 6.3 s mobile, 1.7 s desktop, performance 64/86. Caveat: an in-page PerformanceObserver in my headless runs recorded the hero paragraph, not the image, as the LCP candidate (Chrome may exclude an image that exactly fills the viewport), so the 'LCP element' label rests on the Lighthouse trace the auditor cited; the lazy-loaded, low-priority, upscaled hero is verified either way. Visible softness in ha09-about-m390-hero-detail.png is mild but present.

Measured at 1440 after scrolling. Facts that hold: Suleman and Clemente cards are 834 px tall with photo, 21 to 29 word bio, Read more dialog, email and LinkedIn; Mowgli Frere and Makaiel Javed cards are 439 px with no image, no dialog, 76 and 73 word bios and only a LinkedIn link (Makaiel's card has two LinkedIn anchors, one carrying utm_source=share_via&utm_medium=member_android). Body text: office 0, award 0, finalist 0, 13536901 0, 'Roscap Limited' 0, lender 0, member 0; 'founded' 3 times across hero and story, 'discretion' 3; London appears once but only in Mowgli's biography. The associate does sit under the only heading, 'Leadership Team'. Details wrong: there are not four Teams CMS items; only Suleman and Clemente are .w-dyn-item cards in section.oo-creww, while Mowgli and Makaiel are static Designer .team-card blocks in a separate heading-less section.team-us, so 'add photos in the Teams collection' will not fix them unless they are moved into the collection. 'discipline' appears 2 times, not 3. The National Property Awards 2026 finalist claim has no source in the research folder and I could not verify it; the page simply does not mention any award. Missed by the finding: Mowgli's card title says 'Head of Southern Europe' while his bio says 'Head of Western Europe'. Severity: the section reads as a tidy two-tier layout rather than broken, and the owner wants the site kept simple; thin facts and the mixed card types are a noticeable content and polish issue, so medium rather than high.
